**Taylor Alison Swift** (born December 13, 1989) is an American singer-songwriter. [An influential figure in popular culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_impact_of_Taylor_Swift "Cultural impact of Taylor Swift"), Swift is known for her autobiographical songwriting and artistic reinventions. She is the [highest-grossing live music artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_live_music_artists "List of highest-grossing live music artists"), the [wealthiest female musician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_music_artists_by_net_worth "List of music artists by net worth"), and one of the [best-selling music artists of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best-selling_music_artists_of_all_time "Best-selling music artists of all time").
Swift signed with [Big Machine Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Machine_Records "Big Machine Records") in 2005 and debuted as a [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") singer with the albums _[Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_\(album\) "Taylor Swift \(album\)")_ (2006) and _[Fearless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fearless_\(Taylor_Swift_album\) "Fearless \(Taylor Swift album\)")_ (2008). The singles "[Teardrops on My Guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teardrops_on_My_Guitar "Teardrops on My Guitar")", "[Love Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Story_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Love Story \(Taylor Swift song\)")", and "[You Belong with Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Belong_with_Me "You Belong with Me")" found [crossover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossover_music "Crossover music") success on [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_radio "Country radio") and [pop radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_radio "Pop radio") formats. Her songs began incorporating stronger [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") elements with _[Speak Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now "Speak Now")_ (2010) and [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") styles with _[Red](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_\(Taylor_Swift_album\) "Red \(Taylor Swift album\)")_ (2012). She subsequently recalibrated her artistic identity from country to [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") with the [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop") album _[1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_\(album\) "1989 \(album\)")_ (2014), while ensuing media scrutiny inspired the [trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap_music "Trap music")-imbued _[Reputation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reputation_\(album\) "Reputation \(album\)")_ (2017). Through the 2010s, Swift accumulated the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") number-one singles "[We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_Never_Ever_Getting_Back_Together "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together")", "[Shake It Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shake_It_Off "Shake It Off")", "[Blank Space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blank_Space "Blank Space")", "[Bad Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Blood_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Bad Blood \(Taylor Swift song\)")", and "[Look What You Made Me Do](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Look_What_You_Made_Me_Do "Look What You Made Me Do")".
Shifting to [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") in 2018, Swift released the [eclectic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eclecticism_in_music "Eclecticism in music") pop album _[Lover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lover_\(album\) "Lover \(album\)")_ (2019) and [re-recorded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Re-recorded "Re-recorded") four of her first six albums due to [a dispute with Big Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_masters_dispute "Taylor Swift masters dispute"). She explored [indie folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_folk "Indie folk") on the 2020 albums _[Folklore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folklore_\(Taylor_Swift_album\) "Folklore \(Taylor Swift album\)")_ and _[Evermore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evermore "Evermore")_ , followed by mellower pop subgenres on _[Midnights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnights "Midnights")_ (2022) and _[The Tortured Poets Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tortured_Poets_Department "The Tortured Poets Department")_ (2024), as well as [soft rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_rock "Soft rock") on _[The Life of a Showgirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Life_of_a_Showgirl "The Life of a Showgirl")_ (2025). The singles "[Cardigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardigan_\(song\) "Cardigan \(song\)")", "[Willow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willow_\(song\) "Willow \(song\)")", "[All Too Well (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well_\(Taylor's_Version\) "All Too Well \(Taylor's Version\)")", "[Anti-Hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Hero_\(song\) "Anti-Hero \(song\)")", "[Cruel Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cruel_Summer_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Cruel Summer \(Taylor Swift song\)")", "[Is It Over Now?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Is_It_Over_Now%3F "Is It Over Now?")", "[Fortnight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnight_\(song\) "Fortnight \(song\)")", "[The Fate of Ophelia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fate_of_Ophelia "The Fate of Ophelia")", "[Opalite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opalite_\(song\) "Opalite \(song\)")", "[I Knew It, I Knew You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Knew_It,_I_Knew_You "I Knew It, I Knew You")", and "[Patient Zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patient_Zero_\(song\) "Patient Zero \(song\)")" topped the Hot 100. Her [Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eras_Tour "Eras Tour") (2023–2024) and its associated film, _[Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift:_The_Eras_Tour "Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour")_ (2023), are the [highest-grossing concert tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_concert_tours "List of highest-grossing concert tours") and [concert film of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert_film#Highest-grossing_concert_films "Concert film").
Swift is the only artist to have been named the [IFPI Global Recording Artist of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFPI_Global_Recording_Artist_of_the_Year "IFPI Global Recording Artist of the Year") six times. A record eight of her albums have each sold over a million copies first-week in the US. Publications such as _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ and [_Billboard_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard \(magazine\)") have ranked Swift among the greatest artists of all time. She is the first individual from [the arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_arts "The arts") to be named [_Time_ Person of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Person_of_the_Year "Time Person of the Year") (2023) and the youngest female inductee into the [Songwriters Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songwriters_Hall_of_Fame "Songwriters Hall of Fame") (2026). [Her accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Taylor_Swift "List of awards and nominations received by Taylor Swift") include 14 [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards")—including a record four [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") wins—and a [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award "Primetime Emmy Award"). Swift is the most-awarded artist of the [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards "American Music Awards"), the [_Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Awards "Billboard Music Awards"), and the [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Awards "MTV Video Music Awards"). A subject of [extensive media coverage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_image_of_Taylor_Swift "Public image of Taylor Swift"), she has a global fanbase known as [Swifties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swifties "Swifties").
## Life and career
### Early life
Taylor Alison Swift was born on December 13, 1989, in [West Reading, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Reading,_Pennsylvania "West Reading, Pennsylvania").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-1) She is named after the singer-songwriter [James Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Taylor "James Taylor");[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerone20173-2) her parents chose a unisex name, hoping it would help her succeed in business.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Grigoriadis-2009-3) Her father, Scott Kingsley Swift, was a [stockbroker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockbroker "Stockbroker") for [Merrill Lynch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merrill_Lynch "Merrill Lynch"), and her mother, Andrea Gardner Swift ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Finlay), worked as a [mutual fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutual_fund "Mutual fund") marketing executive.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJepson20131-4) Swift's younger brother, [Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Swift "Austin Swift"), is an actor who manages her film projects.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-5) Taylor and Austin are of Scottish, English, and German descent, with distant Irish and Italian ancestry; they are paternal great-great-grandchildren of [Charles Carmine Antonio Baldi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Carmine_Antonio_Baldi "Charles Carmine Antonio Baldi"), a prominent Philadelphia businessman.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-9) Their maternal grandmother, [Marjorie Finlay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marjorie_Finlay "Marjorie Finlay") ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Moehlenkamp), was an opera singer whose singing in church became one of Swift's earliest memories of music.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer20104-10)
During childhood, Swift spent her [holiday seasons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holiday_season "Holiday season") on a [Christmas tree farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_tree_farm "Christmas tree farm") in Pennsylvania,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-11) and summers at her family's vacation home in [Stone Harbor, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone_Harbor,_New_Jersey "Stone Harbor, New Jersey"), where she occasionally performed acoustic songs at a local coffee shop.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-12) Raised Christian,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-13) she attended preschool and kindergarten at a [Montessori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montessori "Montessori") school run by the [Bernardine Sisters of St. Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernardine_Sisters_of_St._Francis "Bernardine Sisters of St. Francis") before transferring to the Wyndcroft School in [Pottstown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pottstown,_Pennsylvania "Pottstown, Pennsylvania").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-15) When her family moved to [Wyomissing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyomissing "Wyomissing"), she attended [Wyomissing Area Junior/Senior High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyomissing_Area_Junior/Senior_High_School "Wyomissing Area Junior/Senior High School").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-16)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-17) At age nine, she aspired to a career in [musical theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_theater "Musical theater"), performing at local festivals and in Berks Youth Theatre Academy productions,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Interview-19) and traveling regularly to New York City for vocal and acting lessons.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTECarlin201914-21) After watching a documentary about [Faith Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Hill "Faith Hill"), she changed her goal and became determined to pursue a [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") career in [Nashville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee "Nashville, Tennessee").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-22)
At the age of 11, Swift traveled to Nashville with her mother to visit record labels and submit [demo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demo_\(music\) "Demo \(music\)") tapes of [Dolly Parton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Parton "Dolly Parton") and [Dixie Chicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dixie_Chicks "Dixie Chicks") karaoke covers.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-23) She was rejected by all the labels, which led her to focus on songwriting.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-24) She started learning the guitar at the age of 12 with the help of a computer repairman and local musician who assisted Swift in writing an original song.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-25) In 2003, she and her parents started working with the talent manager Dan Dymtrow. With his help, Swift modeled for [Abercrombie & Fitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abercrombie_&_Fitch "Abercrombie & Fitch"), had an original song included on a [Maybelline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maybelline "Maybelline") compilation CD, and was given an [artist development deal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artist_development_deal "Artist development deal") from [RCA Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Records "RCA Records") at 13.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-26)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer201010-27) To help Swift break into the country music scene, her father transferred to Merrill Lynch's Nashville office when she was 14 years old, and the family relocated to [Hendersonville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hendersonville,_Tennessee "Hendersonville, Tennessee").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Widdicombe-2011-28)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Jo_Sales-2013-29) Swift attended [Hendersonville High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hendersonville_High_School_\(Tennessee\) "Hendersonville High School \(Tennessee\)") for two years before transferring to Aaron Academy, which offered homeschooling.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Grigoriadis-2009-3)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-30)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-31)
### 2004–2008: Career beginnings and _Taylor Swift_
[![Taylor Swift speaking into a mic, wearing a white sundress while holding her framed album](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Taylor_Swift_at_Yahoo_2007_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_at_Yahoo_2007_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_at_Yahoo_2007_\(cropped\).jpg)Swift promoting her debut album in 2007
Swift signed with [Sony/ATV Tree Music Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony/ATV_Music_Publishing "Sony/ATV Music Publishing") in 2004; at 14, she became the youngest person in that publishing company's history.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-32) In Nashville, she worked with experienced [Music Row](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_Row "Music Row") songwriters, including [Liz Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liz_Rose "Liz Rose").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-34) Rose and Swift would write songs every Tuesday afternoon after school.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-35) After one year on the development deal, she left RCA Records, which was planning to keep her in development until she turned 18.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-36) Swift made this decision because she wanted to release the songs immediately to ensure that they still resonated with her teenage experiences.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer201012-37)
Swift organized a showcase concert at the [Bluebird Cafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluebird_Cafe "Bluebird Cafe") on November 3, 2004; among the attendees was [Scott Borchetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Borchetta "Scott Borchetta"), a music executive who was planning to establish an [independent record label](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_record_label "Independent record label") called [Big Machine Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Machine_Records "Big Machine Records").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-38) She signed a [recording contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_contract "Recording contract") with Big Machine two weeks after the concert, on the condition that her albums would be self-written;[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-39)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer201021-40) her father purchased a three-percent stake in the company.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-41) The contract was finalized by July 2005, when Swift ended her working relationship with Dymtrow.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-42) She spent four months near the end of 2005 recording her debut album, [_Taylor Swift_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_\(album\) "Taylor Swift \(album\)"), with the producer [Nathan Chapman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Chapman_\(record_producer\) "Nathan Chapman \(record producer\)").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Morris-2006-43)
Swift's debut single, "[Tim McGraw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_McGraw_\(song\) "Tim McGraw \(song\)")", was released in June 2006. She and her mother spent mid-2006 sending promotional copies of the song to [country radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_radio "Country radio") stations across the US.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-44) _Taylor Swift_ was released on October 24, 2006.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer201029-45) On the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") chart, the album peaked at number five and spent 157 weeks on the chart—the longest chart run by an album in the 2000s.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-46) With _Taylor Swift_ , she became the first female country music artist to write or co-write every track on a [platinum-certified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum-certified "Platinum-certified") debut album.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-47) Swift promoted the album with a six-month radio tour and by [opening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opening_act "Opening act") for other country artists, including [Rascal Flatts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rascal_Flatts "Rascal Flatts") in 2006,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Morris-2006-43)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-48) and [George Strait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Strait "George Strait"),[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-49) [Brad Paisley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Paisley "Brad Paisley"),[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-50) and [Tim McGraw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_McGraw "Tim McGraw") and Faith Hill in 2007.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-51) She opened for Rascal Flatts again in 2008,[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-52) when she dated the singer [Joe Jonas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Jonas "Joe Jonas").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-53)
_Taylor Swift_ was supported by four more singles in 2007 and 2008: "[Teardrops on My Guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teardrops_on_My_Guitar "Teardrops on My Guitar")", "[Our Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Song "Our Song")", "[Picture to Burn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picture_to_Burn "Picture to Burn")", and "[Should've Said No](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Should've_Said_No "Should've Said No")". "Our Song" and "Should've Said No" reached number one on the [Hot Country Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Country_Songs "Hot Country Songs") chart; with the former single, Swift became the youngest person to single-handedly write and sing a number-one country single.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-54) "Teardrops on My Guitar" was Swift's breakthrough single on mainstream radio and charts, reaching the top 10 of the [Pop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Songs "Pop Songs"), [Adult Pop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Pop_Songs "Adult Pop Songs"), and [Adult Contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Contemporary_\(chart\) "Adult Contemporary \(chart\)") charts.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-55)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-56) Her next releases were the [Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_music "Christmas music") [extended play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play") (EP) _[The Taylor Swift Holiday Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Taylor_Swift_Holiday_Collection "The Taylor Swift Holiday Collection")_ in October 2007,[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-57) and the [Walmart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walmart "Walmart")-exclusive EP _[Beautiful Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beautiful_Eyes "Beautiful Eyes")_ in July 2008.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-58) Swift became the youngest person to be awarded with the [Nashville Songwriters Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_Songwriters_Association_International "Nashville Songwriters Association International")'s Songwriter/Artist of the Year in 2007.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-59)
### 2008–2010: _Fearless_
[![Taylor Swift wearing a dark strapless dress with her hair pinned up](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/TaylorSwiftApr09.jpg/250px-TaylorSwiftApr09.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TaylorSwiftApr09.jpg)Swift at the 2009 premiere of _[Hannah Montana: The Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Montana:_The_Movie "Hannah Montana: The Movie")_. She had a cameo appearance in the film and wrote two songs for [its soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Montana:_The_Movie_\(soundtrack\) "Hannah Montana: The Movie \(soundtrack\)").
Swift's second album, _[Fearless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fearless_\(Taylor_Swift_album\) "Fearless \(Taylor Swift album\)")_ , was released on November 11, 2008, in North America,[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer201051-60) and in March 2009 in other markets.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-61) _Fearless_ spent eleven weeks at number one on the _Billboard_ 200, becoming her first chart topping album and the longest-running number-one female country album; it was the best-selling album of 2009 in the US.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-62)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-63) The album's lead single, "[Love Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Story_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Love Story \(Taylor Swift song\)")", became the first country song to top the Pop Songs chart, and its third single, "[You Belong with Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Belong_with_Me "You Belong with Me")", was the first country song to top _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard \(magazine\)")_ 's all-genre [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs \(chart\)") chart;[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-64)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-65) both reached the top five of the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") chart and peaked atop the Hot Country Songs chart.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-3-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-2-67) Three other singles—"[White Horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Horse_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "White Horse \(Taylor Swift song\)")", "[Fifteen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteen_\(song\) "Fifteen \(song\)")", "[Fearless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fearless_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Fearless \(Taylor Swift song\)")"—all reached the top 10 of Hot Country Songs.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-2-67) In 2009, Swift opened for [Keith Urban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Urban "Keith Urban")'s tour and embarked on her first headlining concert tour, the [Fearless Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fearless_Tour "Fearless Tour") (2009–2010).[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-68)
_Fearless_ became the most-awarded country album of all time.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-69) It won the three highest awards for a country album: Album of the Year by both the [Country Music Association Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Music_Association_Awards "Country Music Association Awards") and [Academy of Country Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Country_Music_Awards "Academy of Country Music Awards") in 2009, and [Best Country Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Country_Album "Best Country Album") by the [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") in 2010.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-70) At the Grammy Awards, _Fearless_ also won [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year"), and "White Horse" won [Best Country Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Country_Song "Best Country Song") and [Best Female Country Vocal Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Female_Country_Vocal_Performance "Best Female Country Vocal Performance").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-71) Also in 2009, Swift was named Artist of the Year by both the [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2009 "American Music Awards of 2009") and _Billboard_ ,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-72)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-73) and Entertainer of the Year by the Country Music Association Awards, becoming the youngest person to receive the honor.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-74) "You Belong with Me" won [Best Female Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Female_Video "Best Female Video") at the [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Awards "MTV Video Music Awards"). Her acceptance speech was interrupted by the rapper [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West"), [an incident that became the subject of controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_MTV_Video_Music_Awards#Kanye_West%E2%80%93Taylor_Swift_incident "2009 MTV Video Music Awards") and widespread media coverage.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen201633-75)
Swift featured in 2009 on "[Half of My Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_of_My_Heart "Half of My Heart")" by [John Mayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mayer "John Mayer"), with whom she was romantically linked later that year.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-76)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-2014-77) She wrote "[Best Days of Your Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Days_of_Your_Life "Best Days of Your Life")" for [Kellie Pickler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kellie_Pickler "Kellie Pickler"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-78) co-wrote and featured on [Boys Like Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boys_Like_Girls "Boys Like Girls")' "[Two Is Better Than One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two_Is_Better_Than_One "Two Is Better Than One"),[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-79) and wrote "[You'll Always Find Your Way Back Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You'll_Always_Find_Your_Way_Back_Home "You'll Always Find Your Way Back Home")" and wrote and recorded "[Crazier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crazier "Crazier")" for the [soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Montana:_The_Movie_\(soundtrack\) "Hannah Montana: The Movie \(soundtrack\)") of _[Hannah Montana: The appearance.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-80)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-81) She made her acting debut in the 2010 rom-com _[Valentine's ### 2010–2014: _Speak Now_ and _Red_
[![Taylor Swift singing into a mic while playing a guitar, dressed in a purple dress](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Taylor_Swift_2011crop.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_2011crop.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_2011crop.jpg)Swift on the [Speak Now World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now_World_Tour "Speak Now World Tour") in 2011
Swift wrote her third album, _[Speak Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now "Speak Now")_ , entirely by herself.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Caramanica-2010-88) Released on October 25, 2010,[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-89) it debuted atop the US _Billboard_ 200 with over one million first-week copies sold—the highest single-week tally for a female country artist.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-90) Five of its singles—"[Mine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mine_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Mine \(Taylor Swift song\)")", "[Back to December](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_to_December "Back to December")", "[Mean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_\(song\) "Mean \(song\)")", "[Sparks Fly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparks_Fly_\(song\) "Sparks Fly \(song\)")", and "[Ours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ours_\(song\) "Ours \(song\)")"—charted in the top three of Hot Country Songs; "Sparks Fly" and "Ours" reached number one.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-2-67) "Mine" peaked at number three and was the album's highest-charting single on the _Billboard_ Hot 100,[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-91) and "Mean" became its best-selling track.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-92) Swift supported the album with the [Speak Now World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now_World_Tour "Speak Now World Tour") (2011–2012) and its accompanying live album, _[Speak Now World Tour – Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now_World_Tour_%E2%80%93_Live "Speak Now World Tour – Live")_ (2011).[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-93)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-94)
In 2011, Swift was honored as Woman of the Year by _Billboard_ ,[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Roland-2011-95) Entertainer of the Year by both the Academy of Country Music Awards and the Country Music Association Awards,[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-96) and Artist of the Year at the American Music Awards.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-97) She again won Entertainer of the Year at the Academy of Country Music Awards in 2012.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-98) At the [54th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "54th Annual Grammy Awards") in 2012, "Mean" won Best Country Song and [Best Country Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Country_Solo_Performance "Best Country Solo Performance").[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-99) After the release of _Speak Now_ , Swift briefly dated the actor [Jake Gyllenhaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Gyllenhaal "Jake Gyllenhaal").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-2014-77)
On October 22, 2012, Swift released her fourth album, _[Red](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_\(Taylor_Swift_album\) "Red \(Taylor Swift album\)")_ , which she produced with Chapman and several new collaborators, including [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin"), [Shellback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shellback_\(record_producer\) "Shellback \(record producer\)"), [Dan Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Wilson_\(musician\) "Dan Wilson \(musician\)"), [Jeff Bhasker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Bhasker "Jeff Bhasker"), [Dann Huff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dann_Huff "Dann Huff"), and [Butch Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butch_Walker "Butch Walker").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Lewis-2012-100)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Mansfield-2012-101) It debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ 200 with 1.21 million sales, becoming the fastest-selling country album in US history.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-102) _Red_ was Swift's first number-one album in the UK.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-103) During the promotion of _Red_ , Swift was romantically involved with the political heir [Conor Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_family "Kennedy family"), and subsequently the singer [Harry Styles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Styles "Harry Styles").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-2014-77)
[![Taylor Swift wearing a white top and a black fedora hat, smiling with red lips and curly hair](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Taylor_Swift_Red_Tour_2%2C_2013.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_Red_Tour_2%2C_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_Red_Tour_2,_2013.jpg)Swift on [the Red Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Red_Tour "The Red Tour") in 2013
The two most successful singles from _Red_ , "[We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_Never_Ever_Getting_Back_Together "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together")" and "[I Knew You Were Trouble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Knew_You_Were_Trouble "I Knew You Were Trouble")", peaked at numbers one and two on the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-104) Both songs also reached the top five on the [UK singles chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_singles_chart "UK singles chart"), and the former was Swift's first chart topper in the US.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Griffiths-2021-105)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-106) The singles "[Begin Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Begin_Again_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Begin Again \(Taylor Swift song\)")" and "[Red](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Red \(Taylor Swift song\)")" peaked in the top 10 of the _Billboard_ Hot 100,[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-3-66) while "[Everything Has Changed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everything_Has_Changed "Everything Has Changed")" and "[22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/22_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "22 \(Taylor Swift song\)")" reached the top 10 on the UK singles chart.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Griffiths-2021-105) [The Red Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Red_Tour "The Red Tour") ran from March 2013 to June 2014 and became the highest-grossing country tour with revenue of $150.2 million upon completion.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-107) Swift was named Artist of the Year at the American Music Awards in 2013.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-108)
Swift wrote and recorded two songs for [the soundtrack album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hunger_Games:_Songs_from_District_12_and_Beyond "The Hunger Games: Songs from District 12 and Beyond") to the 2012 dystopian film _[The Hunger Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hunger_Games_\(film\) "The Hunger Games \(film\)")_ : "[Eyes Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyes_Open_\(song\) "Eyes Open \(song\)")" and "[Safe & Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safe_&_Sound_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Safe & Sound \(Taylor Swift song\)")".[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-109) The latter, co-written with [the Civil Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Civil_Wars "The Civil Wars") and [T-Bone Burnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-Bone_Burnett "T-Bone Burnett"), won the [Grammy Award for Best Song Written for Visual Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Song_Written_for_Visual_Media "Grammy Award for Best Song Written for Visual Media") in 2013.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-110) She wrote and recorded "[Sweeter than Fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweeter_than_Fiction "Sweeter than Fiction")" for the soundtrack to the 2013 biographical film _[One Chance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Chance_\(film\) "One Chance \(film\)")_ ,[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-111) and featured as a guest vocalist on [B.o.B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B.o.B "B.o.B")'s 2012 single "[Both of Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Both_of_Us "Both of Us")" and Tim McGraw's 2013 single "[Highway Don't Care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highway_Don't_Care "Highway Don't Care")".[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-112)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-113) Her acting roles included a voice acting role in the 2012 animated film _[The Lorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lorax_\(film\) "The Lorax \(film\)")_[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-114) and a supporting role in the 2014 dystopian film [_The Giver_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Giver_\(film\) "The Giver \(film\)").[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-115)
### 2014–2018: _1989_ and _Reputation_
Swift relocated from Nashville to New York City in March 2014 and transformed her image from country to [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") with her fifth album, _[1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_\(album\) "1989 \(album\)")_.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-116)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-117) She produced _1989_ with Martin, Shellback, Chapman, and new collaborators [Jack Antonoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Antonoff "Jack Antonoff"), [Imogen Heap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imogen_Heap "Imogen Heap"), [Ryan Tedder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Tedder "Ryan Tedder"), and [Ali Payami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Payami "Ali Payami").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-118) Released on October 27, 2014, the album spent eleven weeks at number one and one year in the top 10 of the _Billboard_ 200.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-119)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-120) It has sold 14 million copies worldwide, becoming Swift's best-selling album.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Winter-2022-121) Three of _1989_ 's singles—"[Shake It Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shake_It_Off "Shake It Off")", "[Blank Space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blank_Space "Blank Space")", and "[Bad Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Blood_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Bad Blood \(Taylor Swift song\)")"—reached number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100; the first two made Swift [the first woman to replace herself at the top spot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-122) Two other singles—"[Style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Style_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Style \(Taylor Swift song\)")" and "[Wildest Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildest_Dreams "Wildest Dreams")"—peaked at numbers six and five, making _1989_ the first album by Swift to have five consecutive top 10 singles on the Hot 100.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-123)
[![Taylor Swift performing with a mic, wearing a white strapless top, white shorts, and black boots, with fabric connecting her shorts to her boots](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/Taylor_Swift_045_%2817682880264%29.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_045_%2817682880264%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_045_\(17682880264\).jpg)Swift on [the 1989 World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_1989_World_Tour "The 1989 World Tour"), the highest-grossing tour of 2015
Swift supported _1989_ with [the 1989 World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_1989_World_Tour "The 1989 World Tour"), the [highest-grossing tour of 2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_concert_tours#Highest-grossing_tours_by_year "List of highest-grossing concert tours") with $250 million in revenue.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-124) She was named _Billboard_ 's Woman of the Year and received the inaugural [Dick Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark "Dick Clark") Award for Excellence at the American Music Awards in 2014,[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-125)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-126) and "Bad Blood" won [Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year") and [Best Collaboration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_Collaboration "MTV Video Music Award for Best Collaboration") at the MTV Video Music Awards in 2015.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-127) At the [58th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/58th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "58th Annual Grammy Awards") in 2016, _1989_ made Swift the first woman to win Album of the Year twice and also won [Best Pop Vocal Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Pop_Vocal_Album "Best Pop Vocal Album"), while "Bad Blood" won [Best Music Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Music_Video "Best Music Video").[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-128) The most-awarded pop album of all time,[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-129)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-130) _1989_ was selected for preservation in the [National Recording Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Recording_Registry "National Recording Registry") in 2026.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-131)
During the promotion of _1989_ , Swift publicly opposed free [music streaming services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_streaming_service "Music streaming service") and their compensation of artists. She published an [op-ed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Op-ed "Op-ed") in _[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")_ in July 2014 to stress the importance of albums as a creative medium for artists,[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-132) and, in November, removed her discography from ad-supported, free streaming platforms such as [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-133) Big Machine kept her music only on paid, subscription-required platforms.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Christman-2014-134) In a June 2015 open letter, Swift criticized [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music") for not offering royalties to artists during its free three-month trial period and threatened to withdraw her music from the platform,[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-135) prompting [Apple Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") to announce that it would pay artists during the free trial period.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-136) Big Machine returned Swift's catalog to Spotify and other free streaming platforms in June 2017.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-137)
Swift dated the DJ [Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris") from March 2015 to June 2016.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-138) They co-wrote "[This Is What You Came For](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Is_What_You_Came_For "This Is What You Came For")", an [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music") single by Harris featuring [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna"); Swift was initially credited under the pseudonym Nils Sjöberg.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-139) Swift also wrote "[Better Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Better_Man_\(Little_Big_Town_song\) "Better Man \(Little Big Town song\)")", recorded by [Little Big Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Big_Town "Little Big Town") in 2016, which won the Country Music Association Award for Song of the Year.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Ryan-2017-140) She wrote and recorded "[I Don't Wanna Live Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Don't_Wanna_Live_Forever "I Don't Wanna Live Forever")" with [Zayn Malik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zayn_Malik "Zayn Malik") for [the soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifty_Shades_Darker:_Original_Motion_Picture_Soundtrack "Fifty Shades Darker: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack") to the 2017 film _[Fifty Shades Darker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifty_Shades_Darker_\(film\) "Fifty Shades Darker \(film\)")_ ; it peaked at number two on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, the highest for a [_Fifty Shades_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifty_Shades_\(film_series\) "Fifty Shades \(film series\)") single.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-141)
[![Taylor Swift wearing a sparkling snake-patterned bodysuit while performing onstage](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Taylor_Swift_Reputation_Tour1_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_Reputation_Tour1_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_Reputation_Tour1_\(cropped\).jpg)Swift on her [Reputation Stadium Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reputation_Stadium_Tour "Reputation Stadium Tour") in 2018
In April 2016, Kanye West released the single "[Famous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famous_\(Kanye_West_song\) "Famous \(Kanye West song\)")", in which he references Swift in the line, "I made that bitch famous." Swift criticized West and said she never consented to the lyric, but West claimed that he had received her approval, and his then-wife, [Kim Kardashian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Kardashian "Kim Kardashian"), released video clips of Swift and West discussing the song amicably over the phone. Although the clips were proven to be purposefully edited,[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-142) the controversy made Swift a subject of an online "[cancel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancel_culture "Cancel culture")" movement, in which her critics denounced her as a fake and calculating "snake".[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-143) In late 2016, after briefly dating the actor [Tom Hiddleston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Hiddleston "Tom Hiddleston"), Swift began a six-year relationship with the actor [Joe Alwyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Alwyn "Joe Alwyn") and went on hiatus.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-144)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWilkinson2017444-145)
In August 2017, Swift [countersued and won a case against David Mueller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_sexual_assault_trial "Taylor Swift sexual assault trial"), a former [radio jockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_jockey "Radio jockey"), who sued her for damages from loss of employment. Four years earlier, she informed Mueller's employer that he had sexually assaulted her by groping her at an event.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-146) Public controversies influenced Swift's sixth album, _[Reputation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reputation_\(album\) "Reputation \(album\)")_ , which explores themes of fame and finding love amidst the tumultuous affairs.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-147) Released on November 10, 2017,[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-148) _Reputation_ debuted atop the _Billboard_ 200 with 1.21 million US sales and recorded first-week worldwide sales of two million copies.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-149)
_Reputation_ 's lead single, "[Look What You Made Me Do](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Look_What_You_Made_Me_Do "Look What You Made Me Do")", topped the _Billboard_ Hot 100 with the highest sales and streaming week of 2017,[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-150) and was Swift's first UK number-one single.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-151) The singles "[...Ready for It?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/...Ready_for_It%3F "...Ready for It?")", "[End Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End_Game_\(song\) "End Game \(song\)")", and "[Delicate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delicate_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Delicate \(Taylor Swift song\)")" were released to pop radio and all peaked in the top 20 of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-152) In 2018, Swift featured on [Sugarland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugarland "Sugarland")'s "[Babe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe_\(Sugarland_song\) "Babe \(Sugarland song\)")" and embarked on the [Reputation Stadium Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reputation_Stadium_Tour "Reputation Stadium Tour"), which grossed $345.7 million worldwide.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-153)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-154)
### 2018–2021: _Lover_ , _Folklore_ , and _Evermore_
In November 2018, Swift signed a record deal with [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group"), which promoted her albums under [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records")' imprint.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-155) The contract included a provision allowing Swift to maintain ownership of her [master recordings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_recording "Master recording"). In addition, if Universal sold any part of its stake in Spotify, it agreed to distribute a non-recoupable portion of the proceeds to its artists.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-156)[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-157)
[![A portrait of Swift](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/191125_Taylor_Swift_at_the_2019_American_Music_Awards.png/250px-191125_Taylor_Swift_at_the_2019_American_Music_Awards.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:191125_Taylor_Swift_at_the_2019_American_Music_Awards.png)Swift at the [American Music Awards of 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2019 "American Music Awards of 2019"), where she was named Artist of the Decade
Swift's first album with Republic Records and seventh overall, _[Lover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lover_\(album\) "Lover \(album\)")_ , was released on August 23, 2019.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-158) She produced the album with Antonoff, [Louis Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Bell "Louis Bell"), [Frank Dukes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Dukes "Frank Dukes"), and [Joel Little](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Little "Joel Little").[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Catucci-2019-159) _Lover_ peaked atop the charts of such countries as Australia, Canada, Ireland, Mexico, Norway, Sweden, the UK, and the US,[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-160) and was the global best-selling album by a solo artist of 2019.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-161) Three of its singles—"[Me!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me! "Me!")", "[You Need to Calm Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Need_to_Calm_Down "You Need to Calm Down")", and "[Lover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lover_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Lover \(Taylor Swift song\)")"—were released in 2019 and peaked in the top 10 of the _Billboard_ Hot 100. "[The Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Man_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "The Man \(Taylor Swift song\)")" was released in 2020 and charted highly, and "[Cruel Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cruel_Summer_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Cruel Summer \(Taylor Swift song\)")" became a resurgent success in 2023, reaching number one.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-162) Swift promoted _Lover_ with the one-off [City of Lover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Lover "City of Lover") concert, [its accompanying television special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Lover#Video_and_music_releases "City of Lover"), and the live album _[Lover (Live from Paris)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lover_\(Live_from_Paris\) "Lover \(Live from Paris\)")_ , which set the record for the largest vinyl sales week by a live album in the US.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-163)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-bb2025-164)
In 2019, Swift was named Artist of the Decade by the American Music Awards and Woman of the Decade by _Billboard_ ,[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-165)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-166) and became the first female artist to win the MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year for a self-directed video, with "You Need to Calm Down".[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-167) During the promotion of _Lover_ , Swift became embroiled in [a public dispute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_masters_dispute "Taylor Swift masters dispute") with the talent manager [Scooter Braun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scooter_Braun "Scooter Braun") after he purchased Big Machine Records, including the masters of her albums under the label.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Grady-2019-168) Swift said that Big Machine would allow her to acquire the masters only if she exchanged one new album for each older one under a new contract, which she declined.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Grady-2019-168) In November 2020, Swift began [re-recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Re-recording_\(music\) "Re-recording \(music\)") her back catalog to control the licensing of her songs for [commercial use](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synchronization_rights "Synchronization rights").[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-169)
In February 2020, Swift signed a global publishing deal with [Universal Music Publishing Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Publishing_Group "Universal Music Publishing Group") after her 16-year contract with Sony/ATV expired.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-170) During the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), Swift collaborated with Antonoff and [Aaron Dessner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Dessner "Aaron Dessner") on two "sister albums" [surprise-released](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surprise_album "Surprise album") in 2020: _[Folklore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folklore_\(Taylor_Swift_album\) "Folklore \(Taylor Swift album\)")_ on July 24, and _[Evermore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evermore "Evermore")_ on December 11.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-171) Joe Alwyn co-wrote and co-produced several songs under the pseudonym William Bowery.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-172) Both albums incorporate atmospheric [indie folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_folk "Indie folk") and [indie rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_rock "Indie rock") sounds with ### 2021–2023: Re-recordings and _Midnights_
[![Taylor Swift singing into a mic, dressed in a two-piece leather outfit](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/Taylor_Swift_2022_infobox.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_2022_infobox.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_2022_infobox.jpg)Swift performing in 2022
Swift released two re-recorded albums in 2021: _[Fearless (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fearless_\(Taylor's_Version\) "Fearless \(Taylor's Version\)")_ on April 9, and _[Red (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_\(Taylor's_Version\) "Red \(Taylor's Version\)")_ on November 12. Both peaked atop the _Billboard_ 200; the former was the first re-recorded album to do so.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-184) The latter helped Swift become the female musician with the most weeks at number one on the [Top Country Albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Country_Albums "Top Country Albums") chart, and its song "[All Too Well (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well_\(Taylor's_Version\) "All Too Well \(Taylor's Version\)")" became the longest song to top the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-185)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-186)
Swift's tenth album, _[Midnights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnights "Midnights")_ , was released on October 21, 2022.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-The_Guardian-2022-187) _Midnights_ was Swift's fifth album to open atop the _Billboard_ 200 chart with US first-week sales of one million. Its tracks, led by the single "[Anti-Hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Hero_\(song\) "Anti-Hero \(song\)")", made her the first artist to occupy the entire top 10 of the _Billboard_ Hot 100 the same week.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Dailey-2022-188) The album peaked atop the charts of at least 14 other countries, including Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Norway, and Sweden.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-189) Two other singles, "[Lavender Haze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavender_Haze "Lavender Haze")" and "[Karma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karma_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Karma \(Taylor Swift song\)")", both peaked at number two on the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-190)
In 2023, Swift released two re-recorded albums: _[Speak Now (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now_\(Taylor's_Version\) "Speak Now \(Taylor's Version\)")_ on July 7, and _[1989 (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_\(Taylor's_Version\) "1989 \(Taylor's Version\)")_ on October 27. Both debuted atop the _Billboard_ 200, and the former made Swift the female artist with the most number-one albums on the chart.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-191)[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-192) The single "[Is It Over Now?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Is_It_Over_Now%3F "Is It Over Now?")" from _1989 (Taylor's Version)_ reached number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, making Swift the first woman to have three number-one songs from three different albums in a calendar year.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-193) Swift featured on [Big Red Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Red_Machine_\(band\) "Big Red Machine \(band\)")'s "[Renegade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renegade_\(Big_Red_Machine_song\) "Renegade \(Big Red Machine song\)")" and "Birch" (2021),[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-194) [Haim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haim_\(band\) "Haim \(band\)")'s "[Gasoline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gasoline_\(Haim_song\) "Gasoline \(Haim song\)")" (2021),[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-195) [Ed (2022),[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-196) and [the National](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_National_\(band\) "The National \(band\)")'s "[The Alcott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Alcott "The Alcott")" (2023).[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-197) She wrote and recorded "[Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Carolina \(Taylor Swift song\)")" for [the soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where_the_Crawdads_Sing_\(soundtrack\) "Where the Crawdads Sing \(soundtrack\)") to the 2022 mystery film _[Where the Crawdads Sing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where_the_Crawdads_Sing_\(film\) "Where the Crawdads Sing \(film\)")_ In 2022, Swift won Artist of the Year at the American Music Awards[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-202) and Video of the Year for _[All Too Well: The Short Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film "All Too Well: The Short Film")_ , her self-directed short film that accompanies "All Too Well (10 Minute Version)", at the MTV Video Music Awards; _All Too Well_ also won the Grammy Award for Best Music Video.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-203)[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-204) The following year, she again won the MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year with "Anti-Hero",[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-205) became the first musician to rank at number one on _Billboard_ 's year-end top artists list in three different decades (2009, 2015 and 2023),[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-206) and had five out of the 10 best-selling albums of the year in the US, a record since [Luminate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luminate_\(company\) "Luminate \(company\)") began tracking US music sales in 1991.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-207) At the [66th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "66th Annual Grammy Awards") in 2024, _Midnights_ made Swift the first artist to win Album of the Year four times; it also won Best Pop Vocal Album.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-208)
### 2023–present: The Eras Tour, _The Tortured Poets Department_ , and _The Life of a Showgirl_
[![Taylor Swift singing into a mic, wearing a fringed dress](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_Midnights_Era_Set_%2853109799784%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_Midnights_Era_Set_%2853109799784%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_Midnights_Era_Set_\(53109799784\)_\(cropped\).jpg)Swift on [the Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour") in 2023
In March 2023, Swift embarked on [the Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour"), which she conceived as a tribute to her entire discography. The tour spanned five continents through December 2024.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Sisario-2023-209) It exerted [a global cultural, economic, and political impact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_Eras_Tour "Impact of the Eras Tour") and culminated in an unprecedented height of popularity for Swift,[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-210)[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-211)[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-212) Tour became the first tour to gross $1 billion and the [highest-grossing tour in history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_concert_tours "List of highest-grossing concert tours"), with $2 billion in revenue.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-215) [Its 2023 concert film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift:_The_Eras_Tour "Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour") became the highest-grossing of its kind with $250 million,[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-216) and [its 2024 an Era") on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+").[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-218) The events that happened during the tour inspired Swift's eleventh and twelfth albums, _[The Tortured Poets Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tortured_Poets_Department "The Tortured Poets Department")_ (2024) and _[The Life of a Showgirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Life_of_a_Showgirl "The Life of a Showgirl")_ ## Artistry
### Musical styles
With continuous musical reinventions,[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFranssen202290-256) Swift has been described as a "musical chameleon" by journalists and music analysts alike.[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-257)[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-258)[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESloanHarding201921-259) Her discography primarily spans country, pop, and [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music") genres,[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-260) incorporating various styles such as [country pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_pop "Country pop"),[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-261) [country rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_rock "Country rock"), [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop"), indie rock,[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-262) [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock"),[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Petridis-2009-263) [soft rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_rock "Soft rock"),[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-264) and [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop"),[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-265) with elements of [electronica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronica "Electronica"), [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop"), [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B"), and [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music").[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-266)[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Powers-2022-267)[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Powers-2024-268)[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerone201746%E2%80%9349-269) Swift self-identified as a country musician with her first four albums,[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Rosen-2013-270)[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcNutt202077Gasser2019310-271) influenced by 1990s female country artists such as Shania Twain, Faith Hill, [LeAnn Rimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeAnn_Rimes "LeAnn Rimes"), and the Dixie Chicks,[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer201016%E2%80%9318-272) as well as Keith Urban's incorporation of rock, pop, and [blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues "Blues") into country music.[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-273) The albums feature a country pop sound defined by instruments such as the [six-string banjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-string_banjo "Six-string banjo"), [mandolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandolin "Mandolin"), and [fiddle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiddle "Fiddle"), a slight [twang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twang "Twang") in Swift's vocals, and pop rock melodies;[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHughes2017206Perone201733Carlin2019115-274)[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-275) _Speak Now_ expanded this sound with 1970s and 1980s rock influences, including [pop-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop-punk "Pop-punk") and [arena rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena_rock "Arena rock").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Caramanica-2010-88)[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerone201729,_42,_46,_49-276) Some critics argued that country signified Swift's songwriting more than her musical style,[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Petridis-2009-263)[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Jones-2008-277) and accused her of causing mainstream country to stray from its roots.[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHughes2017206-278)[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-279)
_Red_ 's incorporation of [eclectic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eclecticism_in_music "Eclecticism in music") pop and rock styles, including [Britrock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britrock "Britrock"), [dance-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance-pop "Dance-pop"), and [dubstep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubstep "Dubstep"),[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Mansfield-2012-101)[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-280) led to a critical debate over Swift's status as a country musician.[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerone20172-281) Swift then chose 1980s synth-pop to recalibrate her artistic identity, inspired by the music of [Phil Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Collins "Phil Collins"), [Annie Lennox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Lennox "Annie Lennox"), [Peter Gabriel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel "Peter Gabriel"), and [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna "Madonna").[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-282)[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-283) _1989_ , the first album in this direction, incorporates [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") arrangements consisting of dense [synthesizers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizers "Synthesizers") and [drum machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_machine "Drum machine").[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcNutt202079Gasser2019310-284) Swift expanded on the electronic production on her next albums.[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Levine-2019-285) _Reputation_ features a [trap-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap-pop "Trap-pop") production[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-286)[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-287) with elements of hip-hop, R&B, and EDM, and [maximalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximalism_\(music\) "Maximalism \(music\)") arrangements of heavy [bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass_\(sound\) "Bass \(sound\)") and manipulated vocals.[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Powers-2019-288)[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Hyden-2017-289)[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGasser2019310-290) _Lover_ is a pop album[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-291) with a 1980s-influenced sound combining [dream pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_pop "Dream pop"), synth-pop, and pop rock.[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-292)[[292]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-293)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Catucci-2019-159) _Midnights_ and _The Tortured Poets Department_ both have a [minimalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimal_music "Minimal music") synth-pop sound characterized by [analog synthesizers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analog_synthesizers "Analog synthesizers"), sustained [bass notes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass_note "Bass note"), and simple [drum machine patterns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_pattern "Drum pattern"),[[293]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-294)[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-295) although _The Tortured Poets Department_ features a more understated production.[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-296) _The Life of a Showgirl_ incorporates pop and [soft rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_rock "Soft rock"), featuring [new wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_wave_music "New wave music")-leaning compositions and prominent acoustic guitars.[[296]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-297)[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-298)[[298]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDoyle20253-299) When Swift embraced a pop identity, [rockist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockist "Rockist") critics regarded it as an erosion of her country songwriting authenticity,[[299]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcNutt202079Sloan202117Stone202360%E2%80%9361-300) while others considered it necessary for her artistic evolution and defended her as a pioneer of [poptimism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poptimism "Poptimism").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Winter-2022-121)[[300]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESloan202117-301)
Her 2020 albums _Folklore_ and _Evermore_ , described by some critics as "alternative",[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Snapes-2022-302)[[302]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-303) explore indie folk and rock styles. They incorporate a subtle, stripped-back soundscape with orchestrations, muted synthesizers, and [drum pads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_pad "Drum pad").[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Doyle-2021-173)[[303]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Hyden-2021-304)[[304]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGrath202378%E2%80%9379-305) _Evermore_ experiments with varied [song structures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_structure "Song structure"), asymmetric [time signatures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_signature "Time signature"), and diverse instruments.[[305]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-306)[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Barna-2020-307) Critics deemed the indie styles a mature representation of Swift's singer-songwriter status and credited her with popularizing "alternative" music, although there was disagreement over this description.[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGrath202378%E2%80%9379Hibbett202223-308)
