Swift possesses a [mezzo-soprano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mezzo-soprano "Mezzo-soprano") singing voice,[[312]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFulford2014192-313) but she mostly sings in her [alto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alto "Alto") range.[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Powers-2014-314)[[314]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Lambert-2014-315)[[315]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-316) Her [pitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitch_\(music\) "Pitch \(music\)"), [dialect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dialect "Dialect"), and [accent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accent_\(sociolinguistics\) "Accent \(sociolinguistics\)") have undergone many changes throughout her career.[[316]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-317) Reviews of her early country albums criticized her vocals as weak and strained compared to those of other female country singers.[[317]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEProvenzano2018173-318) Defenders of Swift appreciated that she refrained from correcting her pitch with [Auto-Tune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auto-Tune "Auto-Tune") and that she prioritized intimacy and emotion to communicate the messages of her songs with her audience,[[318]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEProvenzano2018173%E2%80%93174Pecknold201681-319) a style that critics have described as conversational.[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Powers-2014-314)[[319]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-320) According to the critic [Ann Powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Powers "Ann Powers"), this singing style is demonstrated through Swift's attention to detail, which conveys an exact feeling—"the subtle adjustment of words and phrases to suggest moods like doubt, hope, and intimacy".[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Powers-2014-314)[[320]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-321)
On _Red_ and _1989_ , Swift's vocals are processed with electronic effects, such as synthesizer tweaking, looping, and multitracking, to accompany the pop production.[[321]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerone201746%E2%80%9348-322)[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Powers-2014-314) Her voice on _Reputation_ and _Midnights_ incorporates hip-hop and R&B influences, resulting in a near-[rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rap "Rap") delivery that emphasizes rhythm and [cadence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadence "Cadence") over melody.[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Powers-2022-267)[[322]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-323) She uses her lower [register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Register_\(music\) "Register \(music\)") vocals extensively in _Folklore_[[323]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-324) and both her lower and upper registers in _Evermore_ ; the [musicologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musicologist "Musicologist") Alyssa Barca described her [timbre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timbre "Timbre") in the upper register as "breathy and bright" and the lower register as "full and dark".[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Barna-2020-307)
Swift's vocals have received more positive assessments since _Folklore_. The critic [Amanda Petrusich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Petrusich "Amanda Petrusich") commented in 2023 that her singing had become richer, with greater clarity and a stronger tone, even in live performances.[[324]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Petrusich-2023-325) _Rolling Stone_ ranked her 102nd on their 2023 list "[The 200 Greatest Singers of All Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone's_200_Greatest_Singers_of_All_Time "Rolling Stone's 200 Greatest Singers of All Time")"; the magazine argued that her breathy timbre allows for a broad range of delivery and commented: "A decade ago, including her on this list would have been a controversial move, but recent releases like _Folklore_ , _Evermore_ , and _Midnights_ officially settled the argument."[[325]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-326) Powers attributed Swift's vocal versatility to her evolving artistry, mentioning her use of hip-hop cadences and country-influenced timbre.[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Powers-2022-267)
### Songwriting
Swift is credited as the lead songwriter on every song she has released and as the sole songwriter on over 60 tracks.[[326]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-327) Her fascination with songwriting began in her childhood; she credited her mother with igniting her early interest by helping her prepare for class presentations,[[327]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-328)[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-329) and she would make up lyrics to Disney soundtrack songs once she had run out of words while singing them.[[329]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-330) Her early influences included the country musicians [Patsy Cline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patsy_Cline "Patsy Cline"), [Loretta Lynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loretta_Lynn "Loretta Lynn"), [Tammy Wynette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tammy_Wynette "Tammy Wynette"), and Dolly Parton;[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Interview-19)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Roland-2011-95) the singer-songwriters [Joni Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joni_Mitchell "Joni Mitchell"), [Melissa Etheridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melissa_Etheridge "Melissa Etheridge"), [Sarah McLachlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_McLachlan "Sarah McLachlan"), and [Alanis Morissette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alanis_Morissette "Alanis Morissette");[[330]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-331)[[331]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-332) and the [emo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emo "Emo") musicians [Pete Wentz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Wentz "Pete Wentz") of [Fall Out Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_Out_Boy "Fall Out Boy") and [Chris Carrabba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Carrabba "Chris Carrabba") of [Dashboard Confessional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dashboard_Confessional "Dashboard Confessional").[[332]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Hiatt-2019-333)[[333]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-West-Songwriting-334) She credited songs by the Dixie Chicks, [Jeannie C. Riley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeannie_C._Riley "Jeannie C. Riley"), and [Kenny Chesney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Chesney "Kenny Chesney") with influencing her approach to narrative songwriting,[[333]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-West-Songwriting-334) and listed [Paul McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney"), [Bruce Springsteen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Springsteen "Bruce Springsteen"), [Emmylou Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmylou_Harris "Emmylou Harris"), and [Kris Kristofferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson "Kris Kristofferson") as career role models for their consistent and evolving songwriting.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Widdicombe-2011-28)[[334]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-335)
Swift considers herself a songwriter first and foremost.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Widdicombe-2011-28)[[335]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESanneh202171-336) She divides her lyrics into three types: "[quill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quill "Quill") lyrics", which feature antiquated words and phrasing; "[fountain pen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fountain_pen "Fountain pen") lyrics", which combine modern storylines with poetic twists and vivid imagery; and "glitter [gel pen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gel_pen "Gel pen") lyrics", which are lively and frivolous.[[336]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-337) Swift has used songwriting to cope with personal experiences; her songs are largely autobiographical and feature narratives that mostly revolve around love and romantic relationships.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Jo_Sales-2013-29)[[337]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-338)[[338]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Faichney-2024-339) In her songwriting process, she would start by identifying an emotion she wanted to convey, and the story and melody would follow.[[339]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-340) Swift has characterized her songwriting as "confessional",[[340]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Vanity_Fair-2013-341)[[341]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-342) and academics have linked her style to [confessional poetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confessional_poetry "Confessional poetry"), noting that her songs reference personal events and express her internal feelings to her audience.[[338]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Faichney-2024-339)[[342]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-343)
Where _Taylor Swift_ and _Fearless_ are rooted in adolescent feelings and detail an optimistic romance inspired by fairy tales, _Speak Now_ reflects Swift's young adulthood, offering newfound wisdom on real-life heartbreak.[[343]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerone201721,_42-344)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Caramanica-2010-88) _Speak Now_ marked the beginning of increasingly intense media speculation about the subjects of her songs, particularly her dating history;[[344]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-345) Swift has described such scrutiny as sexist.[[340]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Vanity_Fair-2013-341) _Red_ explores the tumult of an intense breakup, and _1989_ reflects on failed relationships with a wistful perspective; both incorporate lyrics that hint at sex, reflecting her personal growth.[[314]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Lambert-2014-315) _Reputation_ addresses the public controversies that tarnished Swift's wholesome image while portraying a blossoming romance with intimacy and vulnerability; its extensive references to sex and alcohol marked a departure from the youthful innocence that had informed her past albums.[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Powers-2019-288)[[345]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-346)[[346]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-347) Swift described _Lover_ as a "love letter to love", inspired by her realization of "love that was very real".[[347]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-348)
On _Folklore_ and _Evermore_ , Swift was inspired by [escapism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escapism "Escapism") and [romanticism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanticism "Romanticism") to explore fictional narratives.[[348]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-349) She imposed her emotions onto imagined characters and story arcs, inspired by authors and poets of [romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_literature "Romantic literature") and [modernist literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modernist_literature "Modernist literature") like [F. Scott Fitzgerald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F._Scott_Fitzgerald "F. Scott Fitzgerald"), [Robert Frost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Frost "Robert Frost"), [William Wordsworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Wordsworth "William Wordsworth"), and [Emily Dickinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Dickinson "Emily Dickinson");[[349]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-350)[[350]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJuko2024237,_240Smith202478%E2%80%9380Geary2024135-351) the last of whom was a distant cousin of Swift.[[351]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-352) The albums' characters construct their narratives from fragments of memory, symbolizing the nature of folktales and oral traditions that endure over time.[[352]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurley2024182Juko2024240-353) Swift returned to autobiographical songwriting on _Midnights_ , whose nocturnal ruminations encompass regrets and fantasies informed by her awareness of fame.[[353]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-354)[[354]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Light-2022-355) _The Tortured Poets Department_ explores heartbreak and other themes to extremes, including erotic desire, forbidden love, and escaping the public spotlight,[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Powers-2024-268)[[355]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-356) while _The Life of a Showgirl_ draws on Swift's experiences during the Eras Tour as informed by her fame and romantic life.[[356]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-357)[[357]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-358)
Critical reception of Swift's songwriting has been largely positive,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Widdicombe-2011-28)[[358]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-359)[[359]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Lansky-2023-360) and her melodic compositions have been highlighted for optimizing the [verse-chorus form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verse-chorus_form "Verse-chorus form") with memorable [bridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge_\(music\) "Bridge \(music\)").[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Powers-2014-314)[[360]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-361)[[361]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-362) Several scholars have credited her with taking the confessional singer-songwriter tradition to new heights,[[362]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Sanders-2022-363)[[363]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESemler202314-364) and journalists have variously described her as a "[poet laureate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poet_laureate "Poet laureate")"—of puberty,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Widdicombe-2011-28)[[364]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-365) of romance,[[365]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-366) and of her generation.[[366]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-367)[[367]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-368) In the view of the literary critic [Stephanie Burt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephanie_Burt "Stephanie Burt"), Swift's writing is proficient at "placing inventive, evocative language into pop melodies designed to be sung".[[368]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-369) Some critics have dismissed her "confessional" style as material for [tabloid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabloid_journalism "Tabloid journalism") gossip.[[369]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-370) Objection to the perceived poetic value of her songs, mostly from rockist critics, views her as a pop star using literary subtexts as a commercial ploy, with metaphors that are at times imprecise or self-indulgent.[[370]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHibbett202224%E2%80%9326-371) Scholars have attributed such criticisms to sexism. The musicologist Travis Stimeling argued that while Swift's autobiographical authenticity fits country and rock standards, her mostly male detractors view her depictions of young women's experiences as trivial and unworthy of serious merit.[[371]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStimeling201690%E2%80%9391-372) According to the English-language academic Ryan Hibbett, this gendered criticism bars Swift from receiving the artistic credentials granted to figures such as [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan"), whose romantic themes and occasional literary imprecisions are not as harshly criticized.[[372]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHibbett202225-373)
### Performances and stage

[![Swift singing while playing a piano](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Taylor_Swift_-_Reputation_Tour_Seattle_-_Long_Live-New_Years_Day_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_-_Reputation_Tour_Seattle_-_Long_Live-New_Years_Day_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_-_Reputation_Tour_Seattle_-_Long_Live-New_Years_Day_\(cropped\).jpg)
Swift playing a [six-string banjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-string_banjo "Six-string banjo") on the [Speak Now World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now_World_Tour "Speak Now World Tour") (left, pictured in 2012) and a piano on the [Reputation Stadium Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reputation_Stadium_Tour "Reputation Stadium Tour") (right, 2018)
Swift's concerts feature elaborate settings that incorporate elements of [Broadway theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") and [high tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_tech "High tech").[[373]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-374)[[374]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-375)[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Sisario-2023-209) She does not rely on elaborate choreography and instead emphasizes connecting emotionally with her audience through storytelling and vocal delivery.[[375]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-376) Swift has used special guests and surprise songs or covers as recurring elements of her concerts;[[376]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-377)[[377]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-378) the acoustic "surprise song" segment, which originated during the Speak Now World Tour, has become a fan favorite and one of the most anticipated parts of her shows.[[378]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-379)[[379]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-380)[[380]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-381) Since 2007, she has toured with the same live band.[[381]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-382) She plays four instruments live: guitar (including [electric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_guitar "Electric guitar"), acoustic six-string, and [twelve-string](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelve-string_guitar "Twelve-string guitar")), six-string banjo, piano, and [ukulele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukulele "Ukulele").[[382]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-383)[[383]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-384)[[384]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-385)
Critics have praised her stage presence, stamina,[[385]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-386)[[386]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-387) and ability to bring forth an intimate atmosphere for her audience, even in stadium settings.[[324]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Petrusich-2023-325)[[387]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-388)[[388]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-389) The critic [Sasha Frere-Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sasha_Frere-Jones "Sasha Frere-Jones") hailed her in 2008 as a "preternaturally skilled" entertainer who exerted professionalism with a vibrant energy.[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Jones-2008-277) The journalist [Sam Lansky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Lansky "Sam Lansky") wrote in 2023: "Swift is many things onstage—vulnerable and triumphant, playful and sad—but the intimacy of her songcraft is front and center."[[359]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Lansky-2023-360)
### Videos and filmmaking
Swift emphasizes visuals as a key creative component of her music.[[389]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Ordo%C3%B1a-2022-390) She established her production company, [Taylor Swift Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_Productions "Taylor Swift Productions"), in 2008.[[390]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-391) Her directorial debut was the music video for "Mine", co-directed with [Roman White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_White "Roman White"), in 2010;[[391]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-392) and she developed the concept and [treatment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_treatment "Film treatment") for "Mean" in 2011.[[392]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-393) For the music videos of the _1989_ and _Reputation_ singles, she collaborated extensively with the director [Joseph Kahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Kahn_\(director\) "Joseph Kahn \(director\)") on eight videos;[[393]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-394) among them, she produced "Bad Blood", which won [Best Music Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Music_Video "Best Music Video") at the Grammy Awards in 2016.[[394]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-395) She worked with [American Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Express "American Express") for the "Blank Space" music video (which Kahn directed) and served as executive producer for the interactive app _AMEX Unstaged: Taylor Swift Experience_ , for which she won a [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Interactive Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Interactive_Program "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Interactive Program") in 2015.[[395]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-396)
Swift has [directed 16 of her music videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_videography "Taylor Swift videography").[[396]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-397) "The Man" was her first solo directorial work and made her the first female artist to win the [MTV Video Music Award for Best Direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_Direction "MTV Video Music Award for Best Direction").[[397]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-398) _All Too Well: The Short Film_ , her filmmaking debut, made her the first artist to win the Grammy Award for Best Music Video as a solo director.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Dailey-2022-188)[[398]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-399) In June 2023, Swift was invited to the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences").[[399]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-400) She has cited Joseph Kahn, [Chloé Zhao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlo%C3%A9_Zhao "Chloé Zhao"), [Greta Gerwig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Gerwig "Greta Gerwig"), [Nora Ephron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nora_Ephron "Nora Ephron"), [Guillermo del Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillermo_del_Toro "Guillermo del Toro"), [John Cassavetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cassavetes "John Cassavetes"), and [Noah Baumbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noah_Baumbach "Noah Baumbach") as filmmaking influences.[[389]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Ordo%C3%B1a-2022-390)[[400]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-401)

## Public image
Main article: [Public image of Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_image_of_Taylor_Swift "Public image of Taylor Swift")
[![Taylor Swift wearing a black strapless dress and dark earrings, with curly hair, looking to the side](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/5.3.10TaylorSwiftByDavidShankbone.jpg/250px-5.3.10TaylorSwiftByDavidShankbone.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:5.3.10TaylorSwiftByDavidShankbone.jpg)Swift at the 2010 [_Time_ 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100") Gala
Swift is an enduring figure of 21st-century [popular culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_culture "Popular culture").[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFranssen202290-256) Her career trajectory from a country singer-songwriter to a pop star in the 2000s and 2010s was the subject of extensive commentary.[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Rosen-2013-270)[[455]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcNutt202079-456) Deemed "America's Sweetheart" in her early career, she was described in the press as a "media darling" with a [girl-next-door](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girl-next-door "Girl-next-door")'s polite demeanor and open-hearted conversations.[[456]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFischerSeidman2016529-457)[[457]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Knibbs-2019-458) Swift displayed a feminine image but refrained from the "aggressively sexualized feminist pop" of her contemporaries, leading publications to comment that her [sex appeal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_appeal "Sex appeal") was modest, subtle, and sophisticated.[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Rosen-2013-270)[[458]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-459)[[459]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrown2012176-460) The adolescent themes of Swift's music contributed to her status as a [teen idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_idol "Teen idol"),[[460]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-461)[[461]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-462) although several [feminist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminist "Feminist") authors at the time took issue with her songs about romantic relationships as narrow-minded and detrimental to girls and women, who made up the majority of her fanbase known as [Swifties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swifties "Swifties").[[462]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrown2012176%E2%80%93177Finley2023494-463) Retrospective commentary has largely praised Swift's works for tackling topics of [femininity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femininity "Femininity"), [gaslighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaslighting "Gaslighting"), mistreatment, and [patriarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriarchy "Patriarchy").[[463]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-464)[[464]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Green-2024-465)
Upon recalibrating her artistry to pop music, Swift has identified as a feminist and achieved a [pop icon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_icon "Pop icon") status.[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Levine-2019-285)[[457]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Knibbs-2019-458) In 2013, the author [Jody Rosen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jody_Rosen "Jody Rosen") labelled Swift the "Queen of Pop" due to her popularity that defied traditional boundaries between "genres, eras, demographics, paradigms, trends".[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Rosen-2013-270) Her feminist public image garnered varied reactions from the public, including praise for her success in a male-dominated music industry as an inspiration for girls and women, and criticism that dismissed her feminist adoption as superficial and self-interested.[[465]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFinley2023494-466)
The 2016 dispute with Kanye West bolstered the narrative among Swift's detractors that she was a calculating and manipulative woman despite her sweetheart image, and deepened [their feud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift%E2%80%93Kanye_West_feud "Taylor Swift–Kanye West feud") that has resonated in their respective careers.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen201633-75)[[466]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-467) Her artistic reinventions in the 2020s turned her into an acclaimed singer-songwriter.[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Snapes-2022-302) Buoyed by her enduring pop stardom, she has been recognized as a rare phenomenon that combines the pop star and singer-songwriter archetypes with unprecedented success.[[362]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Sanders-2022-363)[[372]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHibbett202225-373)
Swift is a known [triskaidekaphile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triskaidekaphobia#Lucky_13 "Triskaidekaphobia"), using the number [13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/13_\(number\) "13 \(number\)") in her various works.[[467]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-468) She has also openly embraced the [cat lady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_lady "Cat lady") archetype,[[468]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-469)[[469]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-470) featured or referencing her cats in her works and music videos.[[470]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-471)
## Cultural impact
Main article: [Cultural impact of Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_impact_of_Taylor_Swift "Cultural impact of Taylor Swift")
[![Wax figure of Swift in a white oxford shirt, black hotpants holding a guitar](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Taylor_Swift_wax_figure_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_wax_figure_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_wax_figure_\(cropped\).jpg)Wax figure of Swift at [Madame Tussauds Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madame_Tussauds_Sydney "Madame Tussauds Sydney")
Swift is one of the few artists to have consistently sold millions of albums across two decades despite the post-[album era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album_era "Album era") decline in record sales.[[471]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-472)[[472]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-473) Academics and journalists have therefore described her as "the last pop superstar" and "the last great rock star" of the 21st century.[[473]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFogartyArnold20213-474)[[474]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-475)[[475]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-476) Her commercial strategies for albums and concert tickets have earned her a reputation as a savvy businesswoman,[[476]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-477)[[477]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-478)[[478]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-479) and her use of physical album variants and [Easter eggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_egg_\(media\) "Easter egg \(media\)") have become indicative of music marketing trends.[[479]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerone201724-480)[[480]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-481) The economist [Alan Krueger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Krueger "Alan Krueger") described Swift as an "economic genius".[[481]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-482) _Billboard_ has considered her one of the few artists who can simultaneously achieve chart success, critical acclaim, and fan support, and popularize any sound in mainstream music.[[482]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-483)[[483]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-484)
Swift's success in country music has been credited with popularizing the genre beyond the US and introducing it to adolescent women, a previously ignored demographic.[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Rosen-2013-270)[[484]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-485)[[485]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Roland-2016-486) The critic [Kelefa Sanneh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelefa_Sanneh "Kelefa Sanneh") described her as the biggest country star since [Garth Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garth_Brooks "Garth Brooks"), "and maybe since before him, too".[[486]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESanneh2021190-487) Swift's guitar performances has resulted in increasing sales of guitars among women, which the media dubbed the "Taylor Swift factor".[[487]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-488)[[488]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-489) Her transition from country to pop has been credited as the catalyst for poptimism,[[489]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-490) and her songwriting and musical transitions have been credited with influencing a new generation of artists.[[303]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Hyden-2021-304)[[485]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Roland-2016-486)[[490]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-491)
Swift's enduring popularity, particularly among women, has contributed to her status as a representation of [millennials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennials "Millennials"),[[491]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-492) or, more broadly, of her generation's _[zeitgeist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeitgeist "Zeitgeist")_.[[492]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFogartyArnold20216-493)[[493]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-494) Her fanbase has been described by academics and journalists as one of the most loyal and dedicated.[[494]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-495)[[495]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-496)[[496]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-497) _Time_ 's Cady Lang credited Swift's sustained superstardom to her "savvy manipulation of both the industry and [her] personal brand".[[497]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-498) According to the popular-culture scholars Mary Fogarty and [Gina Arnold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gina_Arnold "Gina Arnold"), Swift is arguably the singular artist "whose story encapsulates many of the urgent conflicts in early twenty-first-century American culture".[[498]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFogartyArnold20215%E2%80%936-499) In a 2024 article for _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ , Joe Coscarelli wrote that her lasting popularity provoked debates comparing her not only to contemporaries like [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake \(musician\)") or Beyoncé, but also to veteran artists like [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles"), [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson"), [Elton John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John "Elton John"), or Madonna.[[499]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-500)
Swift's advocacy for artists' rights and re-recording projects have contributed to industry-wide discourses and reforms.[[500]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-501)[[501]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-502)[[502]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-503) Her artistry and career maneuvers have been the subject of various university courses in literary, cultural, and [sociopolitical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociopolitical "Sociopolitical") contexts.[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFranssen202290-256)[[503]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-504) Swift's legacy has been both embraced and critiqued by groups ranging from feminist and [queer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queer "Queer") communities to [far-right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far-right "Far-right") and religious organizations, and studied by experts across various fields including musicology, literature, sociology, media theory, linguistics, and culture studies.[[504]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-505)
## Wealth and endorsements
Through her management company, TAS Rights Management, LLC, Swift has filed over 300 trademark applications in the US and holds more than 400 registrations worldwide, as of August 2025[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taylor_Swift&action=edit)[[505]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-506) In 2026, Swift filed to trademark her voice and appearance against [AI-generated reproductions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI "Generative AI"), following unauthorized [uses of her likeness in deepfake pornography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_deepfake_pornography_controversy "Taylor Swift deepfake pornography controversy") and presidential election advertisements.[[506]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-507)

## Social activism
Further information: [Political impact of Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_impact_of_Taylor_Swift "Political impact of Taylor Swift")
Swift avoided discussing politics in her early career.[[457]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Knibbs-2019-458) She said that she kept herself as educated as possible but did not want to influence others with her political opinions,[[535]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-536) later attributing her reluctance to the [2003 Dixie Chicks controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dixie_Chicks_controversy "Dixie Chicks controversy") and its impact on country musicians, especially women.[[536]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMoss202245-537) Due to her apolitical stance, she was appropriated by the [alt-right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alt-right "Alt-right") movement in the US, which sparked controversy.[[537]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDriessen20221060-538) Swift voted for [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") in the [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_US_presidential_election "2008 US presidential election") and [2012 US presidential elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_US_presidential_election "2012 US presidential election"), and for [Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton") in the [2016 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_US_presidential_election "2016 US presidential election"); she did not publicly endorse Clinton because she believed that the backlash she was facing at the time could make her endorsement harmful to Clinton's likability.[[538]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Ahlgrim-2024-539)
Since 2018, Swift has been public about her political views and has abandoned her once-apolitical stance.[[539]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-540)[[540]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Dailey-2025-541) She publicly endorsed two [Democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_\(United_States\) "Democratic Party \(United States\)") politicians for the [2018 US midterm elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_US_midterm_elections "2018 US midterm elections"), which resulted in headlines about how she finally dissociated herself from the alt-right and [conservatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States "Conservatism in the United States").[[537]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDriessen20221060-538) In 2020, she urged her fans to check their voter registration ahead of elections, which resulted in 65,000 people registering to vote within one day of her post.[[541]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-542) Swift endorsed the Democratic ticket of [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") and [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris") in the [2020 US presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_US_presidential_election "2020 US presidential election"), and later endorsed Harris and [Tim Walz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Walz "Tim Walz") for the [2024 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_US_presidential_election "2024 US presidential election").[[538]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Ahlgrim-2024-539) She has openly criticized President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") and his policies.[[540]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Dailey-2025-541)[[538]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Ahlgrim-2024-539)
A [pro-choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro-choice "Pro-choice") feminist,[[542]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Snapes-2019-543) Swift is a founding signatory of the [Time's Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time's_Up_\(organization\) "Time's Up \(organization\)") movement against sexual harassment[[543]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-544) and has criticized the [US Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Supreme_Court "US Supreme Court")'s 2022 [decision to end federal abortion rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dobbs_v._Jackson_Women's_Health_Organization "Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization").[[544]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-545) A supporter of [LGBTQ rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_rights "LGBTQ rights"),[[545]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-546) she has donated to [GLAAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD "GLAAD") and the [Tennessee Equality Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Equality_Project "Tennessee Equality Project"),[[546]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-547)[[547]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-548) advocated for the [Equality Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equality_Act_\(United_States\) "Equality Act \(United States\)"),[[548]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-549) and performed during [WorldPride NYC 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WorldPride_NYC_2019 "WorldPride NYC 2019") at the [Stonewall Inn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonewall_Inn "Stonewall Inn"), a [gay rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay_rights "Gay rights") monument.[[549]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-550) Swift has spoken up against [white supremacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_supremacy "White supremacy"), racism, and [police brutality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_brutality_in_the_United_States "Police brutality in the United States") in the US.[[332]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Hiatt-2019-333)[[542]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Snapes-2019-543) She has donated to [March for Our Lives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_for_Our_Lives "March for Our Lives") and supported [gun control and reform in the US](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_politics_in_the_United_States "Gun politics in the United States"),[[550]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-551) donated to the [NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAACP_Legal_Defense_and_Educational_Fund "NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund") and supported the [Black Lives Matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Lives_Matter "Black Lives Matter") movement,[[551]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-552) called for the [removal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Removal_of_Confederate_monuments_and_memorials "Removal of Confederate monuments and memorials") of [Confederate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederate_States_of_America "Confederate States of America") monuments in Tennessee,[[552]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-553) and advocated for [Juneteenth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juneteenth "Juneteenth") to become a national holiday.[[553]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-554)
Swift's political engagements have been met with mixed reception: they have provoked further public discussion of political issues and empowered Swifties, but critics have questioned whether her political alignments were strategic in her career.[[554]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFogartyArnold20217Driessen20221068%E2%80%931069-555) While some publications have argued that Swift's stardom had a significant impact on political involvement in the US, others have viewed her influence as sizable but overstated.[[555]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-556)[[556]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-557) According to the popular culture scholar Simone Driessen, her political impact extended beyond the US to Australia and Europe.[[557]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-558)
## Philanthropy
Swift ranked first on [DoSomething](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DoSomething "DoSomething")'s "Gone Good" list in 2012, 2013, 2014, and 2015.[[558]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-559)[[559]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-560) She received the Star of Compassion from the Tennessee Disaster Services and the Big Help Award from the [Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickelodeon_Kids'_Choice_Awards "Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards") for her "dedication to helping others" and "inspiring others through action".[[560]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-561)[[561]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-562) Especially early in her career, Swift donated to various relief funds following natural disasters. In 2009, she donated $100,000 to the Red Cross to help the victims of the [Iowa flood of 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa_flood_of_2008 "Iowa flood of 2008").[[562]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-563) The same year, she performed at Sydney's [Sound Relief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sound_Relief "Sound Relief") concert, which raised money for those impacted by bushfires and flooding.[[563]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-564) In 2011, Swift used a [dress rehearsal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dress_rehearsal "Dress rehearsal") of her Speak Now tour as a benefit concert for victims of [recent tornadoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak "2011 Super Outbreak") in the US, raising more than $750,000.[[564]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-565) In response to the [May 2010 Tennessee floods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_2010_Tennessee_floods "May 2010 Tennessee floods"), she donated $500,000.[[565]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-566) In 2009, Swift sang at the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")'s [Children in Need](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children_in_Need "Children in Need") concert and raised [£](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pound_sterling "Pound sterling")13,000 for the cause.[[566]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer201065-567) In 2016, she donated $1 million to [Louisiana flood relief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Louisiana_floods "2016 Louisiana floods") efforts and $100,000 to the Dolly Parton Fire Fund.[[567]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-568)[[568]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-569) Swift donated to [food banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_bank "Food bank") after [Hurricane Harvey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Harvey "Hurricane Harvey") struck [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston") in 2017.[[569]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-570) She donated $1 million to [Tennessee tornado relief in 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Nashville_tornado_outbreak "2020 Nashville tornado outbreak") and [again in 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/December_2023_Tennessee_tornado_outbreak "December 2023 Tennessee tornado outbreak"),[[570]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-571)[[571]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-572) as well as $5 million to relief efforts after [Hurricane Helene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Helene "Hurricane Helene") and [Hurricane Milton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Milton "Hurricane Milton") in 2024.[[572]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-573)
She has also donated to [cancer research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer_research "Cancer research"). As the recipient of the [Academy of Country Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Country_Music "Academy of Country Music")'s Entertainer of the Year in 2011, Swift donated $25,000 to [St. Jude Children's Research Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Jude_Children's_Research_Hospital "St. Jude Children's Research Hospital"), Tennessee.[[573]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-574) In 2012, she participated in the [Stand Up to Cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stand_Up_to_Cancer "Stand Up to Cancer") telethon, performing the charity single "[Ronan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronan_\(song\) "Ronan \(song\)")", which she wrote in memory of a four-year-old boy who died of [neuroblastoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroblastoma "Neuroblastoma").[[574]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-575) She has also donated $100,000 to the [V Foundation for Swift is a supporter of the arts. A benefactor of the [Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_Songwriters_Hall_of_Fame "Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame"),[[582]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-583) she has donated $75,000 to Hendersonville High School to help refurbish its auditorium;[[583]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-584) $4 million to the [Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Music_Hall_of_Fame_and_Museum "Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum") in Nashville—the largest donation the museum had received from an artist—to establish the Taylor Swift Education Center, an exhibit and classroom space that opened in 2013;[[584]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-585)[[585]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-586) and $100,000 to the [Nashville Symphony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_Symphony "Nashville Symphony").[[586]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-587) In 2012, Swift partnered with Chegg for Good to donate $10,000 to the music departments of six US colleges.[[587]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-588)
Swift has also provided one-off donations. She has donated items, including signed guitars and concert tickets, to various charities for auction, among them [MusiCares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MusiCares "MusiCares"), [Global's Make Some Noise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global's_Make_Some_Noise "Global's Make Some Noise"), and [Rare Impact Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rare_Impact_Fund "Rare Impact Fund").[[588]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-589)[[589]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-590)[[590]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-591) In 2007, Swift partnered with the Tennessee Association of Chiefs of Police to launch a campaign to protect children from online predators.[[591]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-592) She has also encouraged youth to volunteer in their local communities as part of [Global Youth Service Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Youth_Service_Day "Global Youth Service Day").[[592]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-593) A promoter of children's literacy, Swift has donated money and books to schools across the US.[[593]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-594)[[594]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-595) In April 2018, Swift donated to the [Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rape,_Abuse_&_Incest_National_Network "Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network") in honor of [Sexual Assault Awareness Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_Assault_Awareness_Month "Sexual Assault Awareness Month").[[595]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Dailey-2023-596) She also donated to fellow singer-songwriter [Kesha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kesha "Kesha") to help with [her legal battles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kesha_v._Dr._Luke "Kesha v. Dr. Luke") against [Dr. Luke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Luke "Dr. Luke") and to actress [Mariska Hargitay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariska_Hargitay "Mariska Hargitay")'s [Joyful Heart Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joyful_Heart_Foundation "Joyful Heart Foundation").[[595]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Dailey-2023-596)[[596]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-597)
Swift donated the equivalent of tens of thousands of meals to food banks at each stop of the Eras Tour;[[597]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-598) she also employed local businesses throughout the tour and gave $197 million in [bonus payments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonus_payment "Bonus payment") to her entire crew.[[598]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-599) In February 2024, she donated $100,000 to the family of a woman who died in a [shooting at the Kansas City Chiefs' Super Bowl parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Kansas_City_parade_shooting "2024 Kansas City parade shooting").[[599]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-600) Swift donated $250,000 to Operation Breakthrough in December 2024; the funds were directed to workforce development, childcare, and early learning programs.[[600]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-601) In December 2025, she made donations to eight organizations including MusiCares, Operation Breakthrough, Feeding America, and the [American Heart Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Heart_Association "American Heart Association").[[601]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-602)[[602]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-603)
